title: Global temperature change, 1880 to 2025
summary: Thirty world maps, one every five years from 1880 to 2025, showing how much warmer or cooler each place was than its 1951 to 1980 average.
description: Surface temperature anomaly from NASA's GISS Surface Temperature Analysis (GISTEMP v4), as drawn by NASA's Scientific Visualization Studio: blue where a place was cooler than its 1951 to 1980 average, white where it was near that average, and red where it was warmer, on a scale from minus 4 to plus 4 degrees Celsius. Each map is a 12-month average. NASA labels each map only with its year, so this data set dates it 1 July of that year. Grey is no data: in the early years there were few measurements in many places. The map is flat, so the far north and south take up more of it than they do of the Earth. The numbers are read from the colours of the maps, so they are about, not exact, and the middle colour of a map is not NASA's global average.

source.name: NASA Scientific Visualization Studio, Global Temperature Anomalies from 1880 to 2025 (GISTEMP v4, NASA GISS)
source.credit: NASA's Scientific Visualization Studio. Data provided by Robert B. Schmunk (NASA/GSFC GISS). Visualizer: Mark SubbaRao (NASA/GSFC). Data: GISS Surface Temperature Analysis (GISTEMP v4), NASA's Goddard Institute for Space Studies.

The GISTEMP page states no licence for the data and says graphics need no permission to use elsewhere but their source should be acknowledged, under NASA's media guidance (https://www.nasa.gov/nasa-brand-center/images-and-media/): NASA content used in a factual manner that does not imply endorsement, with NASA acknowledged as the source. Not endorsed by NASA.

regions.name: The whole world
regions.description: The whole map, land and sea, from pole to pole. Grey places have no data and count as missing.

comparisons.question: Which date shows the world warmer than its 1951 to 1980 average?
comparisons.explanation: Date B (about 2025) is mostly red: the middle colour of the map reads about 2 degrees Celsius above normal. Date A (about 1880) is mostly blue and white, about half a degree below normal, with many grey places that had no data. These numbers are read from the colours of the maps, so they are about, not exact.

comparisons.question: Which date shows the world warmer than its 1951 to 1980 average?
comparisons.explanation: Date B (about 2000) reads about 1 degree Celsius above normal in the middle colour of the map; date A (about 1950) reads about half a degree below. These numbers are read from the colours of the maps, so they are about, not exact.
